correctness.rationale: For a length-at-most-n circular factor, at most four cyclic transitions occur. Every mixed XX therefore has exactly three or four transitions, forcing a cyclic two-run root. The four explicit three-transition cases are necessary and sufficient, and the four-transition split cases have exactly min(a,c)-1 or min(b,d)-1 roots when opposite runs match. The monochromatic count follows from maximal run lengths. The sharp maximum is established by a direct parity inequality and constructive witnesses in every residue class. Actual standalone checker replay matched full literal-square sets for exhaustive 5,985 run tuples through length 21 and 300 independent modular-index tests. Finite tests supplement, not establish, the all-length statement.

value.rationale: Four-run binary circles constitute the first nontrivial binary circular class beyond two-run periodic necklaces. Synchronization of opposite runs creates a striking four-way jump in mixed-square counts; all mixed squares are characterized. The sharp all-length maximum is a residue-sensitive natural invariant with explicit extremal witnesses and shows half the sharp universal coefficient. The full infinite classification is useful as a structural benchmark for square-rich circular-word families, not a routine finite computation.
